subject: Request: Transfer committed throughput between exhibits + fee rebalance
messages:
From: Olivia Chen <olivia.chen@acmehealth.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@acmehealth.com>, Acme Health Legal <contracts@acmehealth.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Rebalancing committed throughput across projects - ask

Hi Michael,

Thanks again for the walkthrough last week. We're nearly through internal budgeting, and one ask surfaced from engineering: can we move 200k committed tokens from Exhibit B (internal R&D sandbox) into Exhibit A (prod customer-facing pipelines) for the remainder of the contract term?

Quick context: Exhibit B is no longer in active use for the quarter and our teams want to reallocate budget to support additional production inference for a pilot. They understand moving commits will change the fee profile and are OK with a one-time rebalance.

Can Redwood provide:
- A redlined order form showing the exhibit-level quantity move and the resulting monthly fee change
- A short SOW edit removing the decommissioned module in Exhibit B (we'll need that change captured)
- An estimate of any catch-up charges or credits (if you pro-rate mid-billing-cycle)

We'd like to get this wrapped before our board packet on Nov 20. If you need, I can loop in our procurement lead.

Attachments: current_exhibit_summary.xlsx (not included in this thread)

Best,
Olivia
Olivia Chen
Sr. Procurement Manager, Acme Health

Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 11:07:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Rebalancing committed throughput across projects - ask

Olivia — thanks for the clear ask and the deadline. We can support a transfer of committed tokens between exhibits but there are three items we'll need to coordinate:

1) Order form redline to reflect exhibit quantities and fee recalculation (Sales Ops + Legal)
2) SOW edit to remove the decommissioned Exhibit B module (Product + CS review)
3) Billing impact: whether credits/charges should be pro-rated for the current cycle (Finance)

Laura / Jordan: can you draft a proposed redline (PDF) and updated pricing matrix? Jordan — please include the pro-rata calc for mid-cycle moves.

Karthik: we'll need a fast-turn legal review: exhibit substitutions + signature path. Any custom language we should include around "relocated commitments"?

Grace: CS will need to confirm there are no technical blockers for shifting the capacity. Please flag if the change should trigger migrations or lead time.

Olivia — I'll aim to get the redline to you by EOD Thursday (11/12). If procurement needs a signature via DocuSign we can include that flow.

Cheers,
Michael Grant

Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 16:42:00 -0800
Subject: Draft redline + pricing matrix for Acme rebalancing (attached)

Team / Olivia — attaching the initial artifacts: ACM-OF_v3-redline.pdf (order form with exhibit quantity edits), pricing-matrix-commits.csv (monthly illustration with pro-rata example), and a short SOW markup (SOW-integration-v2-markup.docx).

Summary of approach:
- We reduce Exhibit B committed tokens by 200,000 and increase Exhibit A by the same amount for the remaining term.
- Net monthly fee increases by $4,200 based on Exhibit A's per-token rate; we show a one-time pro-rata adjustment of $1,100 for the current billing window in the pricing matrix.
- We included a clause option in the OF redline: "Relocated Commitments — Customer may reassign committed token quantities across Exhibits no more than twice per contract year subject to Provider approval and an administrative fee." Karthik, please advise on phrasing/acceptability.

Olivia — if that administrative fee is a non-starter, we can remove the clause; it was suggested to prevent frequent churn across exhibits.

Next steps: Legal review + CS sign-off on migration timeline. Jordan

Attachments (stubs): ACM-OF_v3-redline.pdf (PDF, 12 pages, redlines), pricing-matrix-commits.csv (CSV), SOW-integration-v2-markup.docx (Word, markup)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Olivia Chen <olivia.chen@acmehealth.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 09:31:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Draft redline + pricing matrix for Acme rebalancing (attached)

Thanks — I reviewed the redline and the additional clause. High-level feedback:

- The "Relocated Commitments" clause is acceptable but needs clearer limits. Suggested edit: limit to two reassignments per 12-month rolling period and require 30 days written notice prior to the effective date.
- Add a short sentence preserving existing service levels: "Provider's latency and throughput SLOs applicable to Exhibit A shall apply to relocated commitments once the transfer is operationalized." This avoids disputes if Exhibit rates differ because of performance tiers.
- Pro-rata calc is fine — recommend we treat the one-time adjustment as a credit when Exhibit B's reduction exceeds the Exhibit A increase in a billing window; otherwise invoice the delta.

Two legal asks before we send to procurement: 1) remove the administrative fee amount (we can keep the right to charge an administrative fee but leave the amount to be agreed per-execution), and 2) include a short acceptance test window (7 days) post-transfer to allow Acme to validate routing/config.

I'll prepare a redline of Jordan's PDF with these language tweaks and send back by EOD Monday.

Karthik
General Counsel (Contracts), Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.com

From: Olivia Chen <olivia.chen@acmehealth.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 17 Nov 2026 15:02:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Draft redline + pricing matrix for Acme rebalancing (attached)

Michael / team — thanks for the fast turnaround and the clear options. Procurement and Finance reviewed the materials; summary:

- Acme accepts the quantity reassignment as drafted, subject to Karthik's edits around notice and acceptance testing.
- We will not accept an open-ended administrative fee. If Redwood wants an administrative fee, please propose a fixed $500 per reassignment and we'll consider.
- Finance requests that the one-time pro-rata adjustment be reflected as an invoice credit (negative line item) rather than a separate charge — easier for our internal reporting.

Please:
1) Update the OF redline to remove administrative fee amount, or replace with a fixed $500 if Redwood prefers.
2) Add the 30-day notice + 7-day acceptance test language as Karthik suggested.
3) Send a final PDF and a DocuSign link for signature.

We're aiming to have this executed by Nov 23 so it flows into our December billing.

Thanks — Olivia
